Across these realizations, warming produces contrasting subsurface hydrologic responses: Regolith-sourced streamflow generally becomes slightly younger, whereas fractured bedrock-sourced streamflow generally ages. This contrast arises because warming increases evapotranspiration and alters snow accumulation and melt timing, reducing effective recharge and lowering fractured-bedrock saturation. Declining recharge slows water transit and shifts fractured-bedrock-sourced water toward longer flow paths. Our results suggest that warming may reduce fractured-bedrock water renewal, with implications for the buffering role of bedrock water storage and for prolonged retention of legacy contaminants.

articles_hidden.title: An integrative single-cell long noncoding RNA atlas reveals regulatory programs in the pan-cancer tumor microenvironment
articles_hidden.authors: Shiting Wang, Qiheng Qian, Yuting Liu, Yang Ding, Dechang Yang, Xing Zheng, Sijin Cheng, Guoquan Huang, Ge Gao, Jingfa Xiao, Zhang Zhang, Shuai Jiang
articles_hidden.abstract: Long noncoding RNAs (lncRNAs) have been shown as critical components in cancer genomics, yet their functionality and regulation remain elusive. Here, we present an integrative lncRNA atlas covering more than 370,000 cells from 18 cancer types. In addition to multiple lineage- and cellular state transition–associated lncRNAs, we identify a set of lncRNAs that are embedded within cell type–specific regulons, suggesting associations between lncRNA expression and cell type–enriched transcriptional programs. By integrating CRISPR-based functional genomic screens and clinical data, we further prioritize not only CRISPR-supported candidate lncRNAs linked to tumor cell fitness and immune cell state features but also specific lncRNA signatures correlated with patient survival and immunotherapy response.

articles_hidden.title: Non-invasive, high-precision, and independently controllable neuromodulation via optimized multiple temporal interference stimulation
articles_hidden.authors: Kyunghyun Jo, Yeji Kim, Yeonzu Son, Joonhee Won, Woojin Jeon, Joonhyung Kwon, Hyung Jin Choi, Young-Gyun Park, Jong-Seok Kim, Seongjun Park
articles_hidden.abstract: Non-invasive neuromodulation is an important approach in clinical and translational neuroscience, yet existing techniques remain limited in precisely and flexibly targeting spatially distributed brain regions. Temporal interference stimulation (TIS) enabled non-invasive selective targeting; however, conventional implementations lack sufficient spatial focality, steerability, and scalability for network-level modulation. Here, we introduce optimized multiple temporal interference stimulation (omTIS), a computationally optimized framework that achieves high spatial focality, flexible steerability, and scalable control for distributed neuromodulation. Using a multi-electrode architecture, finite element analysis (FEA)–based optimization, and carefully selected multiple carrier frequencies, omTIS generates focal interference envelopes that can be positioned across multiple brain targets, enabling simultaneous and independently controllable multi-focal stimulation with minimal mutual interference. Across simulations, tissue-mimicking phantom experiments, and in vivo mouse studies, omTIS outperformed conventional TIS in spatial selectivity, steering flexibility, and cross-talk-free multi-focal modulation. These results establish omTIS as a scalable platform for precise, non-invasive control of distributed brain networks.

articles_hidden.title: Auditory cortical coding of spectrotemporal modulations is sufficient to support perceptual categorization of speech and music
articles_hidden.authors: Jérémie Ginzburg, Clarisse Gotti, Émilie Cloutier Debaque, Arthur Borderie, Benjamin Morillon, Laurence Martineau, Paule Lessard Bonaventure, Robert J Zatorre, Philippe Albouy
articles_hidden.abstract: Auditory processing is typically described as hierarchical, culminating in neural representation of abstract categories. However, it remains unclear whether category-selective responses in auditory cortex require representational mechanisms beyond the coding of acoustic features or whether the acoustic representations already available in the auditory cortex are sufficient to account for categorization. Here, we test whether cortical coding of spectrotemporal modulation (STM) features is sufficient to support speech-music categorization by combining human intracranial recordings with continuous behavioral judgments of a naturalistic soundtrack in which speech and music occur both separately and simultaneously. We show that temporal and spectral modulation patterns largely characterize speech and music, respectively, and that cortical auditory regions robustly track these features over time, with distinct oscillatory frequency bands preferentially encoding temporal and spectral modulations. Critically, cortical representations of STMs predicted perceptual categorical judgments gathered in an independent sample. Last, speech- and music-related STM representations showed stronger tracking of category-specific acoustical features in left versus right cortical auditory regions, respectively. These findings indicate that the efficient neural coding of acoustical features provides a sufficient basis for the categorical distinction between speech and music and that the temporal and spectral components of this representation are implemented through distinct oscillatory mechanisms.

articles_hidden.title: Monolithic tiered microlithography for stretchable multilayer electronics with high-density, soft, and ultrathin VIAs
articles_hidden.authors: Xinjian Xie, Guangrui Ju, Xiongwei Luo, Shengwei Feng, Hongjiao Li, Yijun Zhang, Wenqian Feng
articles_hidden.abstract: Stretchable multilayer electronics that sustain reliable electrical performance under mechanical deformation are critical for advanced skin-like devices. A remaining challenge is the development of high-density, soft, and ultrathin vertical interconnect accesses (VIAs) that enable reliable electrical interconnection in flexible and stretchable circuits, particularly at small feature sizes. Here, we present a three-dimensional (3D), tier-by-tier photolithography strategy using PEDOT-based conductors and polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS)–based insulators, each photocurable within 10 seconds, to directly pattern soft VIAs and planar interconnects across lithographically defined PDMS openings. Maskless, full-field exposure enables thousands of in-plane and through-plane electrical connections in a single step, bypassing conventional hole-by-hole fabrication and manual VIA-to-pad alignment. The multilayer stack ensures minimal thickness, matched mechanical compliance, and robust conduction and insulation, enabling soft VIAs to preserve cross-layer electrical performance. Integration of lithographically defined cutouts and perforations yields breathable, conformal bioelectronics with skin-friendliness and stable signal acquisition in wearable wireless ECG monitoring. This multilayer 3D electronics platform can be extended to biomolecular sensing in soft organs, where thin, integrated, and stretchable designs are essential.

articles_hidden.title: Nanoparticle-enabled gene delivery for pediatric brain tumors
articles_hidden.authors: Jiayuan Zhu, Helen Forgham, Yu Qin, Xiaodi Li, Xueguang Lu, Sui Wang, David S. Ziegler, Maria Kavallaris, Thomas P. Davis, Ruirui Qiao
articles_hidden.abstract: Pediatric brain tumors are the leading cause of disease-related death in children, yet effective treatment remains a major clinical challenge. These aggressive tumors have limited therapeutic options capable of crossing the blood-brain barrier (BBB) and frequently recur due to genetic or epigenetic alterations and treatment resistance. Gene therapy offers a promising strategy to address these limitations by modifying gene expression, correcting mutations, or introducing functional genes. Nanoparticle (NP) delivery systems facilitate this approach by protecting genetic cargo and enabling BBB penetration and tumor-specific uptake. This review summarizes current genetic engineering strategies and NP-based delivery systems for pediatric brain tumors, including their design principles and delivery mechanisms, highlights key therapeutic approaches under preclinical and clinical investigations, and discusses the major challenges and future directions in NP-mediated gene therapy for pediatric neuro-oncology. By critically evaluating these developments, we aim to underscore the transformative potential of NP-mediated gene therapies in reshaping treatment paradigms and improving outcomes and quality of life for children.

articles_hidden.title: USP8 inhibition suppresses prostate tumorigenesis via promoting RICTOR degradation to inhibit mTORC2 signaling
articles_hidden.authors: Jingchao Wang, Daoyuan Huang, Bo Liu, Weiwei Jiang, Fabin Dang, Li Chen, Tao Hou, Peiqiang Yan, Yihang Qi, Hiroyuki Inuzuka, Lei Li, Wenyi Wei
articles_hidden.abstract: RICTOR plays an essential role in regulating mechanistic target of rapamycin complex 2 (mTORC2) kinase activity, but it remains largely elusive how RICTOR is aberrantly activated in human prostate cancer (PrCa). Here, we identify RICTOR as a substrate of Cullin 3–based ubiquitin ligase adaptor SPOP, an important tumor suppressor in PrCa. SPOP deficiency or cancer-derived SPOP mutations disrupt SPOP-mediated degradation of RICTOR, thereby promoting PrCa progression. Furthermore, we identify USP8 as its upstream deubiquitinase, and inhibition of USP8 specifically suppresses RICTOR/mTORC2 activity without affecting mTORC1. As such, the USP8 inhibitor induces RICTOR degradation concomitant with marked tumor suppression in vivo. Hence, these findings reveal an SPOP-USP8-RICTOR regulatory circuit that underlies PrCa tumorigenesis and provides a rationale for targeting RICTOR via USP8 inhibition as a therapeutic strategy for patients with PrCa.

articles_hidden.title: Reconciling the medical relevance of mitochondrial transplantation in vivo
articles_hidden.authors: Eaman Abay, Joan Sanchez-Gurmaches, Jeffery D. Molkentin
articles_hidden.abstract: Mitochondria transplantation is a proposed therapeutic approach to improve the function of diseased or injured tissue. It has garnered attention and sparked debate.

articles_hidden.title: Hierarchical interfacial anchoring for durable perovskite solar cells
articles_hidden.authors: Jiaxin Wu, Hongzhuo Wu, Zuhong Zhang, Xiaoyu Guan, Jinbo Zhao, Yuting Guo, Zhihao Li, Zirui Li, Tengyu Ma, Ying Tang, Zhe Li, Weiwei Zuo, Jorge Pascual, Bo Hou, Feng Yang, Xiaoli Pan, Yu Wang, Luyao Wang, Lin-Long Deng, Guixiang Li, Luca Sapienza, Antonio Abate, Meng Li
articles_hidden.abstract: Although inverted perovskite solar cells now deliver certified efficiencies approaching their single-junction limits, their practical deployment remains constrained by the thermo-mechanical fragility of buried interfaces under realistic temperature fluctuations. Here, we identify thermo-mechanically driven, stress-accumulation-dominated adhesion failure at self-assembled monolayer-based buried interfaces as a critical failure mode in inverted perovskite solar cells. To address this issue, we propose an interfacial robustness design strategy based on a homometallic halide pretreatment, which constructs a chemically compatible and highly anchorable interfacial environment on transparent conductive oxides to guide the ordered assembly of SAMs. This interfacial treatment increases the density of surface hydroxyl species and enables hierarchical multipoint interfacial anchoring dominated by metal-oxygen coordination, with Cl − induced hydrogen-bonding interactions acting cooperatively, thereby enhancing anchoring robustness and improving tolerance to thermo-mechanical stress accumulation. With this interfacial strategy, the devices achieve a power conversion efficiency of 27.3% (26.9% certified) and retain 94% of their initial efficiency after 400 temperature cycles between −40 and 85°C (ISOS-T-3). These results demonstrate that rational regulation of buried interfacial anchoring architectures can simultaneously enhance device efficiency and long-term operational reliability, offering a viable pathway toward high-efficiency and durable perovskite photovoltaics.

articles_hidden.title: Asymmetric interactions and feast-famine cycles drive chaos in microbial populations
articles_hidden.authors: William F. McLaughlin, Thomas Beardsley, Natalia L. Komarova, Megan G. Behringer
articles_hidden.abstract: Predicting the dynamics of ecological systems is a central challenge in biology. One factor that may limit predictability is ecological chaos. Theory has long suggested that even simple interactions can produce chaos, yet empirical demonstrations in living systems remain scarce. In a two-strain system of Escherichia coli , increasing the duration between resource replenishment reveals transitions from competitive exclusion to chaos, driven by asymmetric ecological interactions and periodic environmental forcing. Guided by these observations, we developed a dynamical systems framework grounded in empirical data that recapitulate the observed dynamics and predicts intermediate ecological states and transitions. Experimental validation of these predictions by implementing the corresponding conditions successfully reproduces the full range of predicted dynamical regimes. Because feast-famine cycles and asymmetric interactions are widespread in nature, our findings provide a model for uncovering the ecological and evolutionary significance of chaos, opening avenues to use resource fluctuation and interaction strength to quantify, monitor, and manipulate complex ecosystem behavior previously interpreted as stochasticity.

articles_hidden.title: Structure and dynamics of the cellular belt driving bacterial gliding motility
articles_hidden.authors: Hanxiong Liu, Yaëlle Aouizerate, Xiangan Liu, Zihe Zhang, Caterina Comas Hervada, Yongtao Zhu, Maxence S. Vincent, Eric Cascales, Bo Hu, Thierry Doan
articles_hidden.abstract: Various bacteria move on solid surfaces through a process known as gliding motility. Gliding bacteria of the phylum Bacteroidota are major ecological players in a wide variety of niches, as commensals or as pathogens. They use the type IX secretion system (T9SS) to transport adhesins to the cell surface, which then travel in a helical pattern to propel the cell. Here, we purified the filament that drives adhesin helical movement and uncovered its structure by cryo–electron microscopy. Live imaging showed that this outer membrane–associated periplasmic belt, built from T9SS core components, is powered by T9SS molecular motors. This structure functions as a moving walkway that conveys outer membrane β barrel protein–adhesin complexes, therefore coupling motor activity to directional surface translation. This study reveals a unique machinery coupling protein secretion with rapid directed movement of membrane-embedded protein complexes.

articles_hidden.title: Flexible megahertz low-power complementary circuits based on nanoscale organic transistors
articles_hidden.authors: Ute Zschieschang, Sabrina Steffens, Karla Cordero-Solano, Hagen Klauk
articles_hidden.abstract: The stringent low-power requirements of wearable electronics systems can be met only by combining p-channel and n-channel transistors in a complementary circuit topology. For circuits based on organic thin-film transistors (TFTs), this calls for improvements in n-channel TFT performance. We report on flexible low-voltage nanoscale n-channel organic TFTs fabricated using a recently developed high-performance small-molecule semiconductor. The TFTs have on/off current ratios greater than 10 8 and subthreshold swings below 200 millivolts per decade. Nanoscale n-channel and p-channel organic TFTs were integrated into inverters that display small-signal gains up to 175, noise margins up to 80%, static power consumption as low as 10 −12 watts, and characteristic signal-delay time constants as short as 60 nanoseconds (at 3 volts). These are the best-performing flexible organic TFT–based complementary inverters reported to date.

articles_hidden.title: Predictive model for nanoparticle incorporation into crystals reveals essential role of interfacial solution structure
articles_hidden.authors: Mingyi Zhang, Kuan-Ting Liu, Dong June Jang, Victorien J. B. Bernat, Ying Xia, Dongsheng Li, Hsin-Mei Kao, Zihua Zhu, Jaehun Chun, Ulrich B. Wiesner, Lara A. Estroff, Elias Nakouzi
articles_hidden.abstract: Control of interfacial phenomena remains limited by incomplete understanding of molecular-scale solution structure at solid-liquid interfaces. We address this challenge by developing and validating a comprehensive analytical model for nanoparticle incorporation during crystallization. Using atomic force microscopy (AFM) probes surface functionalized to be “particle proxies” combined with three-dimensional AFM and force spectroscopy, we measure nanoparticle-calcite crystal binding energies and kinetic barriers associated with interfacial hydration layers. These measurements, together with diffusivities, parameterize a predictive model that is corroborated using surface-functionalized fluorescent silica nanoparticles incorporated into calcite. We show that surface chemistry governs incorporation by reshaping the energy landscape, with amine groups particularly favoring incorporation. Applying this approach to nanoparticles with different topologies further supports our finding that kinetic barriers play a pivotal role in incorporation processes. This synthesis science framework links interfacial solution structure, particle dynamics, and crystallization kinetics, identifying kinetic barriers as a key design principle for engineering bioinspired nanocomposites beyond empirical approaches.

articles_hidden.title: Resolving the black hole sphere of influence in a hyperluminous obscured quasar at redshift 4.6
articles_hidden.authors: Mai Liao, Roberto J. Assef, Chao-Wei Tsai, Manuel Aravena, Román Fernández Aranda, Andrew W. Blain, Tanio Díaz-Santos, Peter Eisenhardt, Jorge González-López, Hyunsung D. Jun, Xiaofeng Li, Guodong Li, Lee R. Martin, Ana Posses, Devika Shobhana, Manuel Solimano, Daniel Stern, Andrey Vayner, Jingwen Wu, Dejene Zewdie
articles_hidden.abstract: Supermassive black holes (SMBHs) imprint gravitational signatures on the matter within their sphere of influence (SoI). Nuclear gas dynamics can hence be used to accurately measure the mass of an SMBH, yet these measurements remain elusive in the early universe. We report the first dynamical measurement of an SMBH mass at z  > 2, based on high–spatial resolution observations of the ionized-carbon 157.7-micrometer and carbon monoxide (12-11) 216.93-micrometer emission lines that resolve the SoI in an obscured quasar at z  = 4.6. The radial profile of the velocity dispersion reveals a clear Keplerian rise, requiring the presence of an ∼6 × 10 9 –solar mass SMBH. We propose that heavily obscured quasars allow such tracers to survive in the inner regions and may be ideal targets for increasing dynamical SMBH mass estimates in the early universe.

articles_hidden.title: Deep ultraviolet bound states in the continuum
articles_hidden.authors: Minsu Jeong, Jihae Lee, Sangwon Lee, Jaeyun Lim, Jihwan An, Junsuk Rho
articles_hidden.abstract: Light confinement is a key strategy for enhancing light-matter interaction, and photonic crystal (PhC) slabs have emerged as a promising resonant platform due to their high Q factors and design flexibility. However, realizing high- Q PhC slabs in the deep ultraviolet (DUV) regime has remained highly challenging due to the lack of suitable materials and limitations in fabrication. In this work, we propose an etchless fabrication strategy based on electron-beam lithography and atomic layer deposition. We demonstrate a shell-type PhC slab in which a low-index photoresist core is conformally encapsulated by a high-index zirconium dioxide shell. Through angle-resolved transmittance measurements, we experimentally observe symmetry-protected bound states in the continuum in the DUV regime and achieve the highest reported Q factor among resonant modes in this spectral range. Furthermore, by comparing conventional bulk-type and shell-type PhC slabs in far-field response, we show that the shell-type structure maintains comparable performance while offering fabrication advantages. These results provide a practical route for realizing high- Q PhC slabs in the DUV and open opportunities for DUV-based molecular sensing and enhanced light-matter interaction applications.

articles_hidden.title: A state-dependent neural circuit resolves approach-avoidance conflict
articles_hidden.authors: Devika Bodas, Şevval Demirci, Olga Procenko, Marine Balcou, Lennart Baumeister, Darryl Segal, Lisa Scheunemann, Carolina Rezaval
articles_hidden.abstract: To survive, animals must balance opportunity and risk, yet how internal motivational state biases this trade-off remains poorly understood. Here, we show that hunger gates avoidance of a noxious stimulus in Drosophila to enable food approach under conflict. Using a behavioral assay in which flies must cross an electric shock barrier to reach food, we find that starvation promotes shock tolerance only when food-related olfactory cues are present. This state- and context-dependent behavioral shift is mediated by a defined neuromodulatory circuit. Leucokinin neurons encode hunger and convey this information to PV5K1 lateral horn output neurons, which integrate internal state signals with food odor cues and suppress shock-responsive FB2B neurons in the ventral fan-shaped body. Accordingly, electric shock-evoked activity in FB2B neurons is suppressed in starved flies exposed to food cues. These findings identify a circuit mechanism by which motivational state gates aversive processing to bias action selection towards goal-directed behavior.

articles_hidden.title: A floss-based platform for native gingival crevicular fluid analysis enables noninvasive systemic and oral health monitoring
articles_hidden.authors: Yixin Yan, Asmita Veronica, Chaoqi Wang, Yue Guo, Anwei He, Minjin Gu, Lu Zhang, Ge Han, Johnson Q. Cui, Saloni Vimal Chandwaney, Jaehyeon Cho, Xuejie Wang, Sin Yu Pau, Sang Jin Lee, Ke Deng, Shuhuai Yao, Hnin Yin Yin Nyein
articles_hidden.abstract: Gingival crevicular fluid (GCF) is a serum-derived biofluid in the gingival sulcus, offering access to systemic metabolic signals and localized oral inflammation. However, its diagnostic utility remains underutilized because native submicroliter volumes cannot be analyzed without specimen pooling and reagent-mediated dilution. We overcome this barrier using a floss-based platform that enables on-demand GCF analysis during routine flossing. The device integrates a dual-fiber system exploiting shear-dependent property for efficient mobilization, liquid-bridge retention, a pyramidal microfluidic sensor stack, and real-time electrofluidic volume correction. This architecture supports multiplexed electrochemical quantification of glucose, uric acid (UA), pH, and H 2 O 2 from native GCF within minutes. In human studies, GCF glucose and UA correlated with capillary blood (glucose: r  = 0.89, UA: r  = 0.78). Site-specific pH and H 2 O 2 levels differentiated inflamed from healthy periodontal sites, correlating with probing pocket depth. By converting a daily hygiene practice into a dual tool for systemic and oral health monitoring, this platform advances comorbidity management for chronic disease populations.

articles_hidden.title: Spheroid-laden hydrogels with dual biomimetic intra- and perispheroidal niches for enhanced bone healing
articles_hidden.authors: Yujin Han, Hyunseok Kwon, Woo Hyuk Jung, Seung Jae Huh, Goen Lee, Dong June Ahn, Heungsoo Shin
articles_hidden.abstract: Stem cell spheroid–hydrogel platforms offer promise for bone defect repair, but implantation-associated oxidative stress, poor vascular ingrowth, and insufficient osteogenic cues limit their clinical translation. Here, we developed dual-NICHE (dual niche-instructive construct for bone healing and engraftment), a gelatin methacryloyl hydrogel containing human adipose–derived stem cell spheroids with spatially distinct intra-/perispheroidal niches. Within a single construct, these two niches provide complementary functions to simultaneously address the key bottlenecks in bone regeneration. The intraspheroidal niche incorporated bone morphogenetic protein-2–immobilized fibers to promote osteogenic differentiation, whereas the perispheroidal matrix contained Sr 2+ –tannic acid nanoparticles (NPs). Upon implantation, the NPs mitigated oxidative stress and supported vascular infiltration. Concurrently, the osteogenic cue promoted differentiation, while the NPs facilitated mineral nucleation and growth, as further supported by molecular dynamics simulations. Together, this spatial integration enhanced vascularized bone formation with a bone volume fraction of ∼13.5% using only 5208 cells per defect in a mouse calvarial model, providing a potentially translatable framework for bone regeneration.

articles_hidden.title: Discovery of volatile- and Fe-rich melts from low-velocity zones above the mantle transition zone
articles_hidden.authors: Hui-Li Zhang, Gang Zeng, Li-Hui Chen, Zhou-Chuan Huang, Zhe Han, Jian-Qiang Liu, Xiao-Jun Wang, Jin-Hai Yu
articles_hidden.abstract: Low-velocity layers atop the mantle transition zone (MTZ) are commonly observed and predicted to comprise volatile- and iron (Fe)–rich melts, yet direct evidence from natural samples remains lacking. Nephelinites from eastern China may preserve such signatures. They contain ultradeep peridotite fragments and show anomalously low potassium (K)/uranium (U) and barium (Ba)/thorium (Th) ratios, indicating derivation from recycled crustal materials in the MTZ, with high-pressure liebermannite residues retaining K-Ba. This study investigates Wuxi nephelinites, eastern China, where seismic tomography images a slab fragment in the MTZ (high-velocity anomalies) and an overlying low-velocity layer. Volatile- and Fe-rich melt inclusions [maximum FeO T content and Cl (chlorine)/K ratio of 21.8 weight % and 0.15, respectively] are identified in these rocks, consistent with predicted compositions of low-velocity zone melts. Phlogopite in unhomogenized inclusions further confirms their volatile-rich nature. Calculated densities of these inclusions exceed that of ambient mantle, thus stabilizing melts atop the MTZ. Sustained volatile influx or melt-rock reaction reduces melt density and triggers upward melt migration, forming nephelinites, providing key petrological record verifying the geophysically detected MTZ molten layer.

articles_hidden.title: Phylogeny explains differences in the crystal structures and chemistry of vertebrate tooth enamel and enameloid
articles_hidden.authors: John T. Fink, Matthew J. Kohn, Myla A. Negrete, Katherine E. Bemis, Melissa T. R. Hawkins, Y. Hsu, Gabriela A. Farfan
articles_hidden.abstract: A phylogenetically diverse suite of modern tooth enamel/enameloid bioapatite from fishes, mammals, and reptiles from 22 species were chemically and structurally analyzed to establish whether crystal structure and chemistry are phylogenetically correlated. Rietveld refinement analysis of x-ray diffraction data suggests variable crystallographic parameters across vertebrates. Coupled chemical data show correlations between the a -axis of bioapatite and the proportions of sodium substitution for calcium, the introduction of vacancies, and carbonate substituting for phosphate (B-type substitution) or channel anions (A-type substitution). Principal component analysis of all variables suggests that a -axis lengths are highly influenced by the introduction of carbonate in both crystallographic sites. Phylogenetic variations in chemistry and structure of enamel/enameloid crystals show how biomineralization processes have changed through evolutionary time with implications for variation in biomineralization processes across vertebrate lineages. The predominant controls on tooth enamel/enameloid crystal structure are phylogeny rather than primary diet or habitat. Crystal structure variations also influence material properties across organisms, which may control how teeth are fossilized.

articles_hidden.title: Dynein-dependent positioning of multiple organelles regulates adaptive gene expression during oxidative stress
articles_hidden.authors: Lucas Albacete-Albacete, Li Jin, Nanami Sato, Marta N. Shahbazi, Simon L. Bullock
articles_hidden.abstract: Cells respond to environmental insults through well-characterized changes to their transcriptome and proteome. The contribution that reorganization of intracellular architecture makes to the adaptive stress response is much less understood. Here, we reveal a conserved spatial response to oxidative stress in which the microtubule motor dynein enhances perinuclear clustering of multiple membrane-bound organelles. These events are triggered by reactive oxygen species and protein kinase C and occur without increased association of dynein with its activator dynactin, pointing to a noncanonical mechanism for stimulating retrograde transport. Using a chemically inducible system for dispersing individual organelles, we show that perinuclear localization of multiple compartments potentiates oxidative stress–induced gene expression, with distinct genes depending on inputs from either combinations of organelles or individual compartments. Together, these findings implicate positioning of multiple membrane-bound compartments in gene expression regulation and identify coordinated organelle trafficking by dynein as an additional regulatory layer in the cellular stress response.

articles_hidden.title: THERM-D uncovers distinct neural mechanisms separating morning and evening body temperature rhythms in Drosophila
articles_hidden.authors: Tadahiro Goda, Olivia M. Lopez, Richard Ramolete, Nils Reinhard, Nick Ulle, Ayumi Fukuda, Yujiro Umezaki, Kazim Rizvi, Madison G. Aikawa, Roslyn Catiis, Victoria Z. Marquez, Richard Ngo, Nikita C. Raj, Cora Fisher, Gregory T. Bui, Jalen Lee, Charlotte Helfrich-Förster, Taishi Yoshii, Fumika N. Hamada
articles_hidden.abstract: Animal body temperature rises throughout the day and peaks in the evening, a pattern conserved across diurnal endotherms and ectotherms. However, the mechanisms driving the robust body temperature rhythms (BTRs) remain largely unclear. Here, we developed a machine learning–based platform, Temperature Homeostasis Evaluation of Rhythmicity in Model Drosophila (THERM-D), enabling continuous, high-throughput analyses of BTR. Using THERM-D, we identified robust BTR patterns reflecting flies’ morning and evening behaviors and revealed the function of CRYPTOCHROME (CRY)–negative clock neurons. About half of all clock neurons lack CRY, yet their functions are only partially understood. Gal4 drivers targeting CRY-negative neurons demonstrated that these neurons control the morning temperature rise. We further show that separate clock circuits regulate morning and evening BTRs. Thus, THERM-D elucidated the role of CRY-negative clock neurons in BTR and provides a powerful platform for uncovering mechanisms underlying circadian temperature homeostasis.

articles_hidden.title: Steering nanometric reductive-oxidative Fenton-like cycle for PFAS mineralization
articles_hidden.authors: Yichuan Wang, Jianfeng Zheng, Xinchun Ye, Tianlin Zhou, Ting Li, Menghan Feng, Dahong Huang, Seunghyun Weon, Menachem Elimelech, Xiaoxiong Wang, Shuo Zhang
articles_hidden.abstract: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFASs), known as “forever chemicals,” have highly stable C─F bonds that render them resistant to destruction by conventional water treatment processes. Here, we developed a destructive technology that does not require external photo-, electro-, or heat energy input, relying simply on Fenton-like cycles (peroxymonosulfate activation) under nanometric spatial confinement. Unlike the ordinary activation process, confinement shielded peroxymonosulfate radicals ( S O 5 • − ) from external quenching and enabled them to remain active for reductive defluorination. Coupled with oxidative sulfate radicals ( S O 4 • − ), this process unlocked a synergistic “reduction-oxidation” destruction pathway. Specifically, the catalyst was designed by planting single-atom cobalt on MXene nanosheets, whose interlaminar confinement directed efficient PFAS mineralization via alternating α-carbon defluorination (by S O 5 • − ) and decarbonization (by S O 4 • − ). We further constructed a Fenton bed that allowed highly efficient and cost-effective treatment of PFASs in complex water matrices. Our findings underscore the promising potential of nanoconfinement in driving reductive-oxidative Fenton-like cycles toward efficient PFAS mineralization.

articles_hidden.title: Engineering interfacial nucleation and growth for long-life, ultrahigh-rate anode-free sodium batteries
articles_hidden.authors: Chunlin Xie, Jiaming Zhang, Shengfang Liu, Junhui Lu, Peiyu Wang, Xianghui Meng, Yougen Tang, Xiaobo Ji, Haiyan Wang
articles_hidden.abstract: The practical application of anode-free sodium batteries (AFSBs) is limited by the poor reversibility of sodium plating and stripping on current collectors. Here, we show that conventional graphite unexpectedly regulates sodium plating and stripping through a dynamic, interactive interface that enables multidimensional charge transport. This behavior arises from the combination of ultrafast mixed ion-electron transport, reversible ether solvent cointercalation, and the anisotropic flake architecture of graphite, which together promote efficient charge exchange and edge-dominant nucleation. The resulting adaptive interface forms an ultrathin, mechanically robust SEI that stabilizes sodium plating and stripping across a wide current density range (1C to 10C). Ampere hour–level anode-free pouch cells based on this design exhibit an initial Coulombic efficiency of 92.3%, retain 84.9% capacity after 1100 cycles at 3C, and display exceptional safety characteristics, including minimal temperature rise at high rates and no thermal runaway during nail penetration. These results establish a platform for controlling interfacial metal nucleation and growth in AFSBs.

articles_hidden.title: Cortical population codes for embedding sensory inputs into the prior context
articles_hidden.authors: Iacopo Hachen, Sebastian Reinartz, Alisea Stroligo, Alejandro Pequeno-Zurro, Mathew E. Diamond
articles_hidden.abstract: According to theories of the brain as a predictive network, perceptual decisions result from integrating incoming sensory inputs with prior experience. A neuronal population implementing this form of computation must not only retain information about past events but also combine this information with current sensory evidence. To examine how this integration occurs, we recorded extracellular activity from both primary sensory cortex and a target frontal region in rats performing stimulus categorization. Psychophysical analysis showed that judgments were history dependent. Sensory cortex represented the current stimulus largely independently of prior stimuli and failed to account for the history dependence seen in behavior. In contrast, frontal cortex embedded current input within a representation of prior sensory information, with the two variables aligned along partially overlapping coding dimensions. This mechanism predicted choice bias in the behavioral data and involved a disproportionate contribution from putative fast-spiking units. These findings suggest distinct contributions of sensory and frontal cortical regions to predictive processing and point to frontal cortex as a potential site where sensory history may be integrated with incoming evidence to influence perceptual decisions.

articles_hidden.title: Subclonal evolution can shape the transition toward a sarcomatoid phenotype in pleural mesothelioma
articles_hidden.authors: Maya Arnould, Jean-Baptiste Assie, Clément Meiller, Ruth Sequeiros, Sandrine Imbeaud, Amélie Roehrig, Camille Boano, Delphine Le Corre, Sophie Mouillet-Richard, Lucie Poupel, Julien Lavergne, Véronique Hofman, Paul Hofman, Sarah Humez, Arnaud Scherpereel, Françoise Le Pimpec-Barthes, Jessica Zucman-Rossi, Christophe Blanquart, Marie-Claude Jaurand, Sylvie Lantuejoul, Theo Z. Hirsch, Diane Damotte, Didier Jean
articles_hidden.abstract: A better understanding of intratumor heterogeneity in pleural mesothelioma (PM) is crucial to implementing precision medicine for this deadly cancer. Using single-cell RNA sequencing approaches on tumor samples and derived primary cell lines, we defined four phenotypic cell types, related to overall survival in larger bulk cohorts: epithelioid, sarcomatoid, intermediate, and nondifferentiated. Some tumor samples showed intratumor phenotypic heterogeneity, associated with subclonal evolution, in which sarcomatoid cells can emerge from parental cells with an intermediate phenotype following the acquisition of copy number variations. Subclones were conserved in cell lines and retained their specific phenotypes, suggesting high phenotypic heritability. Spatial transcriptomics illustrated the link between phenotypic and subclonal evolution, showing that subclonal cells were colocalized and exhibited specific morphologies within the tumor tissue. Our study provides a comprehensive single-cell profiling of PM tumor cells and reveals a link between phenotypic evolution, clonal architecture, and tumor spatial organization.

articles_hidden.title: The interferon-gamma response pathway is a targetable driver of FSHD muscular dystrophy progression
articles_hidden.authors: Beatrice Biferali, Federica Del Prete, Mara Salomè, Jose Manuel Garcia Manteiga, Reza Alemohammad, Miriam Mombellardo, Maria Pannese, Emanuele Mocciaro, Francesca Torri, İlker Eren, Elisabetta Ferraro, Dicle Ballikaya, Beatrice Ciurli, Arianna Votta, Daniele Campolungo, Daniel C. Turner, Monica Canepari, Roberto Bottinelli, Gabriele Siciliano, Serpil Eraslan, Giulia Ricci, Davide Gabellini
articles_hidden.abstract: Facioscapulohumeral muscular dystrophy (FSHD) is a leading neuromuscular disorder caused by the aberrant expression of the transcription factor double homeobox 4 (DUX4) in skeletal muscle. While DUX4 is normally restricted to early embryonic development, its reactivation in FSHD triggers chronic inflammation and progressive muscle degeneration. However, the precise molecular links between DUX4 and persistent immune activation remain poorly understood. Here, we show that DUX4 induces a viral mimicry-like pathway that is fundamentally uncoupled from canonical type I interferon (IFN) activation. Instead, DUX4 establishes a non-canonical innate immune state dominated by IFN-γ signaling, providing a mechanistic explanation for the non-resolving inflammation characteristic of the disease. We demonstrate that while IFN-γ treatment alone is sufficient to recapitulate key DUX4 pathogenic effects, its inhibition rescues muscle inflammation and halts disease progression in FSHD models. These findings define a “skewed viral mimicry” process driven by a disease-specific transcription factor and identify IFN-γ as a primary therapeutic target for tissue-informed immunomodulation in muscular dystrophy.

articles_hidden.title: Chromatin loci move coherently due to spatially correlated fluctuations
articles_hidden.authors: Janni Harju, Mattia Ubertini, Deepthi Kailash, Po-Ta Chen, Pierre Ronceray, Luca Giorgetti, Thomas Gregor, David B. Brückner
articles_hidden.abstract: From enhancer-promoter communication to DNA repair, essential genome functions require chromosomal loci to encounter each other. While live-cell imaging enables direct measurement of pairwise locus dynamics, a quantitative framework for interpreting them is lacking. Here, using imaging data from Drosophila embryos and mouse stem cells, we show that nearby loci diffuse relative to each other far more slowly than expected from polymer chain–mediated effects. We propose that this slowdown is caused by spatially correlated fluctuations (SCFs) which couple loci via the nucleoplasm. We theoretically predict how these fluctuations scale with space, time, and genomic separation and confirm these predictions using live-cell imaging. Using polymer simulations, we demonstrate that while spatially correlated equilibrium noise fails to reproduce the observed SCF scalings, coupling the polymer to actively driven flows recapitulates the experimental statistics. Consistently, we experimentally show that SCFs couple locus motion across chromosomes and that their magnitude depends on adenosine 5′-triphosphate (ATP)–dependent activity and cohesin-mediated loop extrusion. By reducing encounter frequencies while prolonging encounter durations, SCFs generate a trade-off with direct implications for gene regulation. Our results provide a quantitative framework for chromatin dynamics, revealing how nuclear activity governs chromatin encounters in living cells.

articles_hidden.title: Light-guided photophosphorylation nanorobot rescues injured cardiomyocytes via in situ bioenergetic restoration
articles_hidden.authors: Tingting Yue, Meng Mao, Xiankun Lin, Yang Huang, Qiang He
articles_hidden.abstract: Myocardial injury is a leading cause of death worldwide and is accompanied by profound mitochondrial bioenergetic dysfunction in impaired cardiomyocytes. Restoring cellular bioenergetic homeostasis could be a promising strategy to promote cardiac repair; however, current clinical adenosine triphosphate (ATP) injection therapies yield limited efficacy due to the inability to achieve in situ, targeted delivery. Here, we develop a photoactivated phosphorylation nanorobot engineered to rescue impaired metabolism via targeted, in situ ATP synthesis within cardiomyocytes. These Janus photophosphorylation nanorobots are fabricated through mechanical extrusion–assisted phase separation, enabling the asymmetric integration of chromatophore-coupled F o F l -ATPases. Under structured near-infrared irradiation, the nanorobots exhibit synergistic F o F l -ATPase rotation, which simultaneously drives active propulsion and high-yield ATP catalysis. Following targeted internalization and efficient lysosomal escape, the nanorobots achieve deep penetration into injured myocardial tissue. Intracellularly, the localized elevation of ATP rebalances the NAD + /NADH ratio, suppresses pathological mitochondrial permeability transition pore (mPTP) opening, and mitigates calcium ion overload—collectively restoring mitochondrial integrity and promoting functional myocardial recovery. This self-propelled, bioenergy-restoring nanoplatform represents a rationally designed strategy for targeted therapy of energy-deficient cardiomyopathies.

articles_hidden.title: Somatostatin 6, a master maternal mRNA driving early development
articles_hidden.authors: Jie Chen, Jing Gao, Ting Nie, Lu Liu, Huiming Yuan, Rute S. T. Martins, Adelino V. M. Canario
articles_hidden.abstract: Vertebrate genomes contain six somatostatin (SST) gene family members, of which only SST1 and cortistatin (CORT or SST2) are present in mammalian genomes. These genes encode peptides that predominantly exert inhibitory effects on growth, metabolism, reproduction, and the immune system. However, their roles in nonmammalian vertebrates remain poorly understood. Here, we examined zebrafish sst6 ( sst6.2 ) loss of function and discovered that maternally inherited sst6 mRNA is vital for embryonic cleavage and gastrulation. Its absence impaired calcium release from stores, calcium wave propagation, F-actin assembly, furrow ingression, and overall embryonic development. Moreover, maternal sst6 mRNA is crucial for degrading maternal mRNAs, for calcium-dependent phosphorylation of Stat3 and Smad1/5, and for activating zygotic gene transcription, including pou5f1 , nanog , and sox2 , as well as downstream pluripotency factors. This suggests that maternal sst6 mRNA acts as a master regulator of early development, a function likely conserved in other vertebrates.

articles_hidden.title: Seasonal effects of simulated marine heatwaves on temperature-dependent growth performance
articles_hidden.authors: Rhian Evans, Ben P. Harvey, Bayden D. Russell
articles_hidden.abstract: Marine heatwaves (MHWs) are increasingly longer and more frequent globally, but the cumulative impacts of multiple events on organism performance remain poorly understood. Using thermal performance models, we simulate the effects of simple seasonal MHW scenarios on the predicted growth of 36 mariculture species across the western Pacific Ocean. Simulations suggested that winter MHWs could generally benefit growth, while summer MHWs produced generally negative impacts, especially at higher latitudes where species experience summer growth periods. When combined, winter and summer MHW scenarios indicated a cumulative negative effect for most species. Vulnerability was highest at the warm- and cold-range edges of species’ distributions. These simulations suggest that temperature-dependent growth may be closely linked to the seasonal timing and frequency of extreme events, with multi-season MHWs posing potential challenges for mariculture species in the future. Our simulations highlight the importance of considering multi-season impacts in climate adaptation strategies.

articles_hidden.title: Tunable spectral correlations of highly multimode visible light via broadband quantum frequency conversion
articles_hidden.authors: Federico Presutti, Logan G. Wright, Shi-Yuan Ma, Tianyu Wang, Benjamin K. Malia, Tatsuhiro Onodera, Peter L. McMahon
articles_hidden.abstract: Multimode squeezed states of light are a resource for achieving quantum advantage in computing and sensing, where spatial or temporal modes have been the experimental norm. In our experiments, we generated highly frequency-multimode infrared quantum light and showed how adiabatic frequency conversion can be used to convert the quantum state to visible wavelengths while concurrently manipulating the joint spectrum by realizing a configurable many-port frequency-domain beamsplitter unitary transformation. We report near-unity efficiency quantum frequency conversion over a bandwidth >45 terahertz, which allowed us to measure the state with an electron-multiplying CCD (EMCCD) camera-based spectrometer, at noncryogenic temperatures. The parametric amplification and conversion of >400 frequency modes yielded an overall mean of ∼700 visible photons per shot and photon statistics consistent with squeezing. Our work shows how many-mode quantum states of light can be generated, manipulated, and measured with efficient use of hardware resources, motivating the use of frequency encoding in quantum optics.

articles_hidden.title: Hydrogen radical-participating spatiotemporal sequential therapy via hypoxia aggravation for hypoxia-amplified immunotherapy
articles_hidden.authors: Jinlei Peng, Hui Wang, Zheng Li, Jiayi Xu, Zongyan Du, Nan Cheng, Wei Li, Yadong Na, Dahai Hou, Yunzhu Xu, Xianli Yang, Yuyan Tan, Dongdong Sun, Haibo Cheng, Weiwei Tao
articles_hidden.abstract: The hypoxic characteristics of the tumor microenvironment and endogenous antioxidant defenses compromise the efficacy of oxygen-consuming oxidative therapy, positioning oxygen-free reductive stress as a new paradigm in tumor treatment. Nevertheless, the immunosuppressive characteristics of hypoxia and reductive stress pose significant challenges for advancing reductive stress-induced immunotherapy. Here, we constructed a hydrogen radical (H•) generator synergistically activated by near-infrared light and thiols, and first elucidated that photocatalytic H•-mediated reductive stress can elicit a robust antitumor immune response via the H•-featured mechanism. Nanoplatform HA@UFTL was engineered using lactate oxidase as an ideal H• partner, with the synergistic contribution enabling cross-amplified antitumor immunotherapy. The H•-participating spatiotemporal sequential strategy highlights a triple spatiotemporal sequential cascade, including dual sequential hypoxia exacerbation, sequential oxidative-reductive stress, and sequential organelle damage. By aggravating rather than alleviating hypoxia, HA@UFTL overcomes immunosuppression induced by hypoxia and reductive stress with H• as a universal building block, providing new insights for hypoxia-based immunotherapy.

articles_hidden.title: Unblockable communication with gravity
articles_hidden.authors: Andrew J. Groszek, Charles W. Woffinden, Michael D. Harvey, Andrew G. White, Matthew J. Davis
articles_hidden.abstract: All modern wireless communication technologies are based on electromagnetism. However, electromagnetic signals are readily susceptible to screening and blocking, so their availability cannot be guaranteed in adverse environments. This raises a fundamental question: Can information be transmitted through an unblockable channel? Here, we show that gravity, under physically realistic conditions, offers such a path. We propose and implement a wireless communication protocol in which a broadcaster encodes a binary message by moving a mass, while a receiver detects the resulting gravitational signal with a gravimeter. We validate this scheme experimentally, successfully transmitting a gravitational message a distance of ≈0.7 meters through a brick wall at a rate of 1 bit per minute. These results establish gravity as a viable platform for practically unblockable communication.

articles_hidden.title: Complex IV maturation coordinates postnatal mitochondrial and metabolic development
articles_hidden.authors: Milica Popovic, Alfredo Cabrera-Orefice, Lea Isermann, Marijana Croon, Aleksandra Zecic, Jana Meisterknecht, Yasmin Alameldin, Vidyarashmi Hanehalli, Triinu Siibak, Christian Frezza, Ilka Wittig, Aleksandra Trifunovic
articles_hidden.abstract: The perinatal heart undergoes a rapid metabolic transition from glycolysis to fatty acid oxidation that requires extensive mitochondrial remodeling, yet the molecular checkpoints that coordinate this process remain poorly defined. Using temporally resolved proteomics and complexome profiling of developing mouse hearts from late gestation through early postnatal life (E18.5 to P10), we identify a discrete developmental window in which respiratory chain architecture is remodeled to enable metabolic commitment. Complex IV (CIV) emerges as a central structural determinant of this transition, undergoing isoform-specific reassembly and transient suppression at birth before incorporation into mature respiratory supercomplexes. We identify the CIV subunit COX7C as a developmentally regulated determinant of CIV maturation, with its abundance increasing during maximal respirasome assembly and the switch to fatty acid oxidation. Loss of COX7C impairs terminal CIV maturation, prevents incorporation of heart-specific isoforms, and destabilizes the respirasome organization. Notably, this defect causes a selective secondary failure of complex I completion, demonstrating that respirasome formation is required for catalytic CI maturation in vivo. Consequently, cardiac-specific COX7C deficiency fails to complete the perinatal metabolic transition, leading to the collapse of fatty acid oxidation, activation of nucleotide and serine–glycine–one-carbon metabolism, attenuated activation of the mitochondrial integrated stress response, and a metabolically and structurally compromised state unlikely to support the increasing energetic demands of the postnatal heart. Together, these findings define a developmentally timed, CIV-dependent assembly step that couples respiratory chain assembly to postnatal cardiac metabolic fate and provide a temporal framework for mitochondrial maturation in the developing heart.

articles_hidden.title: Neuromorphic self-aware wings for embodied-intelligent bionic flying microrobotics
articles_hidden.authors: Hao Zheng, Xu Zeng, Yao Tan, Changliu He, Cheng Tu, Haitao Deng, Yu Song, Yan Wang, Beomjoon Kim, Yuan Lin, Xiaosheng Zhang
articles_hidden.abstract: Flying insects achieve robust proprioception and agile flight control using distributed mechanoreceptors on their wings, but current bionic flying microrobots rely heavily on external sensors for state monitoring. Typical sensing solutions including offboard vision or surface-mounted devices inevitably sacrifice either flight autonomy or payload capacity. Inspired by insect wing mechanoreception, we introduce an embodied neuromorphic self-sensing paradigm that eliminates this tradeoff by enabling intrinsic, aerodynamics-maintenance proprioception in flapping-wing systems. Instead of treating the wing solely as a propulsive structure, we reengineer it into a self-contained sensory organ capable of autonomous motion monitoring and health state awareness. We develop an interface charge field mapping model that decouples complex local wing motions, enabling dynamic three-dimensional reconstruction of wing deformation. Building on this theoretical foundation, a conformal bionic mechanoreceptor is directly grown on the wing surface via layered sensitive units. By synergistically combining physics-driven kinematic feature extraction with machine learning, the system achieves real-time fault diagnosis and closed-loop aerodynamic-loss compensation. We do not add sensors to the wing, we make the wing itself the sensory organ. This embodied self-sensing paradigm establishes a new principle for structural intelligence in bionic robotics, offering a promising path toward autonomous, self-aware, and robust miniature flying systems.

articles_hidden.title: Dual-modality photoacoustic and optical coherence tomography imaging simultaneously tracks transplanted stem cells and their viability
articles_hidden.authors: Sumin Park, Wei Qian, Jeff Folz, Van Phuc Nguyen, N. Dayanthi Perera, Wei Zhang, Abigail T. Fahim, Yannis M. Paulus, Xueding Wang
articles_hidden.abstract: Monitoring transplanted cell viability in vivo, noninvasively remains a considerable challenge. By using multiwavelength photoacoustic microscopy powered by a reactive oxygen species (ROS)–responsive contrast agent, we can relatively and semiquantitatively assess and longitudinally monitor the viability of human-induced pluripotent stem cell–derived retinal pigment epithelium (hiPSC-RPE) cells in vivo. The contrast agent comprises colloidal chain-like gold nanoparticle (CGNP) clusters conjugated with IR775c, a heptamethine cyanine dye that undergoes selective oxidative quenching under elevated ROS conditions associated with cellular death (CGNP-IR775c). Dual-wavelength photoacoustic microscopy at 620 and 775 nanometers provides self-calibrated ratiometric measurements that enable relative viability assessment, distinguishing healthy from nonviable cell populations. In vitro studies demonstrated that CGNP-IR775c exhibited biocompatibility and showed dose-dependent ROS sensitivity across physiologically relevant H 2 O 2 concentrations. hiPSC-RPE cells labeled by CGNP-IR775c were subretinally transplanted into living rabbit eyes and longitudinally monitored for 2 weeks, showing that laser-induced oxidative stress produced measurable photoacoustic signal changes that were consistent with the viability status of the transplanted cells. The imaging technology developed here provides a practical solution for noninvasive, longitudinal, and semiquantitative assessment of the transplanted cell viability in vivo, and may contribute to ophthalmology cell-based therapy in both preclinical and clinical settings.

articles_hidden.title: The importance of organics in hydrothermal environments: A synchrotron laboratory study
articles_hidden.authors: Laura E. Jenkins, Stephen P. Thompson, Eamonn T. Connolly, Celine Beck, Sarah J. Day, Lucy K. Saunders
articles_hidden.abstract: The icy moon Enceladus has hydrothermal plumes that are of astrobiologic interest as they could provide conditions to sustain life or allow for its origin. To understand the geology of hydrothermal environments on icy moons, a carbonaceous asteroid simulant similar to the material Enceladus may have accreted from was subjected to conditions analogous to that of its seafloor. The sample environment used allowed high-resolution in situ synchrotron x-ray diffraction data to be collected during the experiment. Mineral reactions were observed as they occurred. Multiple mineral reactions had a large dependence on organic matter. Organics catalyzed the breakdown of aluminosilicates and dissolved pyrite. Melanophlogite and pyrrhotite were also formed as a result of organics being present. This study reveals that organics can have a large impact on mineral reactions and likely play an important role in the geology of hydrothermal vents on icy moons, which have an abundance of organics.

articles_hidden.title: Dynamic nuclear pores dictate the emergence of lamina-associated domains and UV protection during embryogenesis
articles_hidden.authors: Fei Xu, Adrián Fragoso-Luna, Itai Sharon, Angelo L. Angonezi, Dania Camila Pulido Barrera, Kamaludeen Mariyath Nibrasul Haque, Cristina Tocchini, Can Eser, Hiroshi Kimura, Ohad Medalia, Peter Askjaer, Susan E. Mango
articles_hidden.abstract: Lamina-associated domains (LADs) are large heterochromatin domains tethered to the nuclear periphery. LADs organize genome architecture, replication, repair, and transcription, but their formation during development is not well understood. Here, we use DamID and single-cell imaging to analyze embryonic LAD biogenesis in Caenorhabditis elegans . In early embryos, abundant nuclear pore components prevent heterochromatin formation at the lamina, and DNA positioned there is transcriptionally active. Over time, pore components decline, enabling LADs to form; auxin-mediated pore depletion induces precocious LADs. Nuclear basket component npp-21 /Translocated Promoter Region is not required, distinguishing embryonic LAD biogenesis from LADs in differentiated cells. Functionally, LADs confer protection against UVB radiation: Older embryos concentrate DNA damage at the nuclear periphery and survive UVB, whereas early embryos accumulate damage throughout nuclei and die, unless shielded by their mothers in utero. Within the embryo, damage is concentrated in upper, ultraviolet-facing cells, while underlying cells are shielded, suggesting that the Bodyguard effect operates at the organismal level. These findings identify embryonic dissipation of nuclear pores as a key step in embryonic LAD biogenesis, enabling older embryos to withstand environmental challenges.

articles_hidden.title: Immune infiltrate predicts response to αPD1/αCTLA4 but not αPD1 and distinguishes programs of primary resistance in metastatic melanoma
articles_hidden.authors: Amy Y. Huang, Kelly P. Burke, Marc C. Glettig, Ryan Porter, Peter Fatouros, Jonathan M. Li, Lynn Meiger, Valeria Rosado, Shuyun Xu, Jiekun Yang, Emily Robitschek, Natalie Vokes, Cora Ricker, Giuseppe Tarantino, Jiajia Chen, Tyler J. Aprati, Yiwen He, Cassia Wang, Doris Fu, Li-Lun Ho, Kyriakitsa Galani, Gordon J. Freeman, Elizabeth I. Buchbinder, F. Stephen Hodi, Christine G. Lian, Manolis Kellis, Genevieve M. Boland, Arlene H. Sharpe, David Liu
articles_hidden.abstract: While immune-checkpoint blockade (ICB) has revolutionized treatment of metastatic melanoma, the identification of robust biomarkers to predict the relative efficacy of single versus combination ICB has been challenging. We performed a meta-analysis of eight cohorts of patients treated with anti–PD-1 ( n  = 290), anti–CTLA-4 ( n  = 175), and combination anti–PD-1/anti–CTLA-4 ( n  = 51) with pretreatment tumor sequencing and clinical annotations. Surprisingly, the increased response rate to combination anti–PD-1/anti–CTLA-4 compared to anti–PD-1 monotherapy was observed only in highly immune infiltrated tumors, and not in immune-low tumors. Stratifying tumors by high or low frequency of immune cells also distinguished context-dependent programs of primary resistance to single and combination ICB. Notably, hypoxia-related pathways were enriched in nonresponders to anti–PD-1 ICB in immune-high, but not immune-low, tumors. Using an independent cohort of patients with scRNA-seq data, we observed that correlates of hypoxia were associated with increased stromal tumor receptor-ligand interactions. As proof of concept, selective inhibition of HIF-2α, a component of the hypoxia pathway and highly expressed in endothelial cells and fibroblasts, in combination with anti–PD-1, controlled tumor growth in mouse models of highly immune-infiltrated tumors but not poorly immune-infiltrated tumors. Our work demonstrates how stratification by tumor immune characteristics and clinical features can lead to the rational discovery of novel therapeutic targets.

articles_hidden.title: Pten regulates neurogenic radial glia lineage progression and tunes neocortical astrocyte production in Mapk1/3 -dependent pathway
articles_hidden.authors: Osvaldo A. Miranda, Ximena Contreras, Florian M. Pauler, Amarbayasgalan Davaatseren, Nicole Amberg, Carmen Streicher, Ana Villalba, Yuwei Chen, Anna Heger, Corentine Marie, Bassem A. Hassan, Thomas Rülicke, Simon Hippenmeyer
articles_hidden.abstract: The cerebral cortex consists of immense numbers of diverse cell types derived from radial glial progenitor (RGP) cells. How RGPs generate appropriate quantities of distinct cell types to safeguard a brain of correct size is not well understood. However, genetic aberrations in human, including mutations in PTEN , lead to cortical malformation such as macrocephaly, albeit with unknown etiology. Here, we used mosaic analysis with double markers (MADM)–based clonal analysis and single-cell phenotyping to decipher the role of Pten in RGP lineage progression during cortical ontogeny. Although neurogenic RGP lineage progression was altered and projection neuron production doubled in the absence of Pten , cortical astrogenesis was drastically increased. Through epistasis experiments, we show that the loss of Pten uncouples astrogenesis from essential growth factor signaling hubs, funneling into MAPK (mitogen-activated protein kinase). Collectively, our results suggest that Pten regulates RGP lineage progression with distinct sequential functions in corticogenesis to safeguard the emergence of a correctly sized cortex.

articles_hidden.title: Cross-domain encoding models reveal shared and domain-specific neural representations across language and mathematics
articles_hidden.authors: Tomoya Nakai, Rieko Kubo, Shinji Nishimoto
articles_hidden.abstract: Whether language and mathematics rely on shared or distinct neural representations remains unresolved in cognitive neuroscience. Here, we combined latent features from a large language model with functional magnetic resonance imaging encoding models to test cross-domain generalization in 32 participants performing sentence comprehension and calculation tasks. Cross-domain prediction identified cortical regions showing partially shared representations, most consistently in the left area 55b, while control analyses suggested that these effects could not be fully explained by low-level visual or task-general factors. Domain-specificity contrasts revealed stronger language-related prediction in the left superior temporal sulcus and angular gyrus and math-related prediction in the left precentral sulcus and bilateral intraparietal sulci. Model-weight analyses revealed distinct weight profiles associated with shared and domain-specific prediction patterns. Cross-domain regions also exhibited task-dependent functional coupling with language- and math-related networks. Together, these findings suggest that language and mathematics involve partially shared neural representations alongside domain-specific cortical organization, helping reconcile previous contrasting views on their neural basis.

articles_hidden.title: Spatially multiplexed microneedle biosensors for low-abundance protein biomarker monitoring in dermal interstitial fluid
articles_hidden.authors: Ravi Jada, Ying Liu, Yuxiong Liu, Heng Guo, Yin-Yuan Huang, Yixuan Wang, Md Saifur Rahman, Jack Delk, Arda Aidan Arikan, Ayse Akcan Arikan, Srikanth Singamaneni, Limei Tian
articles_hidden.abstract: Microneedle (MN) biosensors offer a minimally invasive approach for molecular analysis of interstitial fluid (ISF), but multiplexed detection of low-abundance protein biomarkers remains limited by poor spatial functionalization and analytical sensitivity. Here, we introduce a high-resolution transfer-printing strategy that functionalizes individual MNs with distinct biorecognition elements on a single patch, enabling simultaneous capture and on-needle analysis of multiple protein biomarkers. Combined with plasmonic-enhanced ultrabright fluorescent nanolabels, the platform enables sensitive multiplexed quantification of low-abundance immune and kidney function biomarkers in mouse models and human subjects. ISF biomarker concentrations showed strong correlations with corresponding plasma levels, supporting the physiological relevance of MN-based measurements. The MN patch enabled painless, blood-free sampling with rapid skin recovery and no irritation. This scalable platform provides a versatile approach for minimally invasive biomarker profiling and may facilitate frequent disease monitoring and timely clinical decision-making.

articles_hidden.title: Structural basis of Anopheles mosquito salivary protein complexes implicated in malaria transmission
articles_hidden.authors: Tiantian Su, Shiheng Liu, Adeline E. Williams, Eric Calvo, Z. Hong Zhou
articles_hidden.abstract: Successful malaria transmission by Anopheles mosquitoes depends on Plasmodium development within the mosquito midgut and subsequent sporozoite invasion of its salivary glands. Salivary proteins, notably Saglin and likely salivary gland surface proteins (SGS4 and SGS5), were suggested to play roles in these processes, but the lack of their structures has hindered our understanding of the underlying molecular mechanisms. In this study, we carried out biochemical and mass spectrometry analyses of salivary gland extracts and demonstrate that Anopheles gambiae SGS4 and SGS5 bind Saglin and other SG1 (salivary gland 1) proteins. Cryo-EM structure of the Saglin-SGS4 complex reveals that Saglin homodimerizes through coiled-coil interactions and disulfide bonds and engages longitudinally with SGS4. Comparisons among SG1-SGS complexes show that SG1 proteins share a conserved architecture, and SGS proteins adapt conformationally to bind different SG1 partners of varying lengths. To our knowledge, our findings uncover the first native mosquito salivary protein complexes that likely facilitate malaria transmission and highlight potential vector targets for blocking malaria transmission.

articles_hidden.title: GenNA: Conditional generation of nucleotide sequences guided by natural language annotations
articles_hidden.authors: Yi Shen, Guangshuo Cao, Jianghong Wu, Dijun Chen, Cong Feng, Ming Chen
articles_hidden.abstract: Deciphering the mapping between biomolecular sequences and complex biological functions is a central challenge in genomics. While existing generative nucleotide models capture sequence distributions, they lack explicit access to gene-associated biological semantics, limiting semantics-guided design. Here, we present GenNA, a generative nucleotide foundation model guided by natural language annotations. Pretrained on a multimodal nucleotide-text corpus spanning 2221 eukaryotic species (∼416 billion characters), GenNA internalizes relationships between sequence syntax and functional semantics within a unified autoregressive framework. Without explicit rule-based supervision, GenNA yields distinguishable perplexity responses to sequence-annotation mismatches, mutational variants, and species-label perturbations. Furthermore, across diverse generation tasks, GenNA produces statistically plausible nucleotide sequences consistent with target semantics, structural constraints, and species contexts. Overall, GenNA provides a versatile framework for controllable nucleotide generation, establishing a practical route to integrate functional descriptions with sequence design.

articles_hidden.title: Dissecting the molecular triggers of early and late long-term potentiation
articles_hidden.authors: Rui Wang, Michaela Schweizer, Kristina Ponimaskine, Christian Schulze, Christine E. Gee, Thomas G. Oertner
articles_hidden.abstract: The brain stores information by changing the strength of its synapses, a process that has at least two phases: Late long-term potentiation (L-LTP) is thought to result from the consolidation of early LTP (E-LTP), just as long-term memory requires the prior establishment of short-term memory. Recently, inhibitory avoidance experiments under CaMKII inhibition have challenged this notion, demonstrating long-term fear memory without measurable short-term memory. Here we use optogenetic activation and inhibition of CaMKII during induction of spike-timing-dependent potentiation (tLTP) to dissect the signaling pathways. While CaMKII activation in CA1 neurons was sufficient to induce E-LTP, growth of the postsynaptic density and spine neck expansion, we found that CaMKII-induced LTP does not give rise to L-LTP. Conversely, inhibition of CaMKII during tLTP induction prevented E-LTP, but FOS and L-LTP were still expressed, driven by CaMKK and PKMζ. Thus, both long-term memory and L-LTP form in the absence of CaMKII activation.

articles_hidden.title: Disulfiram inhibits pyroptosis and apoptosis through multiple complementary mechanisms
articles_hidden.authors: Han Yu, Elliott M. Bernard, Stefania A. Mari, Tetiana Serdiuk, Kristyna Pluhackova, Michele M. Nava, Upnishad Sharma, Matilde Lucioli, Wenhui Cheng, Jack Kuipers, Martin Fussenegger, Paola Picotti, Sebastian Hiller, Petr Broz, Daniel J. Müller
articles_hidden.abstract: Gasdermins (GSDMs) execute pyroptosis by forming lytic pores in the plasma membrane that release IL-1 cytokines and promote cell swelling and membrane rupture. Their key roles in infection, inflammation and cancer make GSDMs attractive therapeutic targets. Here we systematically investigate how disulfiram, an approved drug for treating alcoholism, inhibits pyroptosis and identify multiple complementary mechanisms. First, disulfiram inhibits processing of procaspase-1 to caspase-1. Second, disulfiram inhibits caspases from processing human GSDMD to release the lytic N-terminal domain (GSDMD Nterm ). Third, disulfiram structurally modifies GSDMD Nterm . Fourth, disulfiram partitions into membranes, where it remains embedded, changes membrane properties and prevents GSDMD Nterm insertion. Similarly, disulfiram blocks intrinsic apoptosis by inhibiting procaspase-3 activation, caspase-3 cleavage of human GSDME, and GSDME Nterm pore formation. Furthermore, we show that two other GSDMD inhibitors, necrosulfonamide and dimethyl fumarate also inhibit GSDM-induced cell death through multiple complementary mechanisms. These multilevel inhibitory mechanisms deepen our understanding of strategies to target GSDM-mediated cell death pathways.

articles_hidden.title: A membrane-guided strategy for optimizing proton exchange membrane fuel cells via spatially controlled acid distribution
articles_hidden.authors: Jingjing Lin, Yilin Chen, Jisong Hu, Muzi Xu, Dong Liu, Jinwu Peng, Lei Wang
articles_hidden.abstract: Efficient regulation of phosphoric acid (PA) distribution is vital for advancing high-temperature proton exchange membrane fuel cells. PA migration from the membrane into the catalyst layer (CL) enhances proton accessibility but compromises membrane conductivity, highlighting the need to balance acid distribution within the membrane electrode assembly. Here, we propose a membrane-guided strategy enabling systematic evaluation of PA distribution effects and identification of a favorable acid content range. By designing side chain–grafted polybenzimidazole (PBI) membranes with abundant acid-binding sites, we achieve tunable acid doping levels and regulate PA partitioning through acid-polymer interactions. To compare PA accumulation, we introduce the mass ratio of phosphorus to platinum in the CL (PA CL /Pt CL ) as a semiquantitative descriptor of CL acid content and use distribution of relaxation times analysis to decouple its influence on ohmic resistance, oxygen reduction kinetics, and oxygen transport. We identify a favorable PA CL /Pt CL range of approximately two to three under the present conditions, while the nearly twofold enhancement over OPBI highlights coordinated control of membrane transport and the CL acid state.
